item.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until US meets conditions
item.description: Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said on Sunday that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, according to the state-linked news agency Nournews. item.title: Brazil votes in polarised presidential election between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Brazilians began voting on Sunday in a general election that pits left-wing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro. About 160 million registered voters are eligible to cast ballots in the election…

item.title: Supreme Court opens new term with major cases on climate, guns, immigration; Alito hints at retirement
item.description: This term continues a structural shift in how the Supreme Court operates: emergency ('shadow docket') rulings, which are fast, largely unexplained, and skip full briefing or oral argument, now outnumber traditional merits decisions reached after months of litigation. item.title: Q3 Earnings Season Opens With Record Corporate Optimism; Early Results Beat Estimates
item.description: The third-quarter earnings season kicked off this week with a record level of corporate optimism about future profits, according to MarketWatch. More companies than ever have expressed upbeat outlooks for their bottom lines as reporting begins.

item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak: clinical trial tests experimental pill to prevent infection
item.description: More than 250 participants have been enrolled in a clinical trial in eastern Congo testing an experimental antiviral pill designed to prevent Ebola infection after exposure, as the country battles its deadliest outbreak of the disease.
